meta.title: Stable Diffusion and Latent Diffusion
meta.thesis: Stable Diffusion and Latent Diffusion is practical when learners can apply it to this concrete case: A product team edits background scenes quickly using latent diffusion instead of pixel-space generation. By the end, they should be able to build or review latent diffusion mental model with prompt, latent, decoder, and safety review, measure usable variations per prompt iteration, and catch the failure where latent edits preserve unwanted artifacts because the mask or prompt was underspecified.

modules.title: Latent space is a compressed image workbench
modules.sub: The denoising happens in a smaller representation.
modules.summary: Latent diffusion trades pixel-space cost for practical generation.

blocks.title: Denoise the blueprint before printing the poster

spans.text: Problem anchor: a course author wants many visual drafts without huge pixel-space compute. Latent diffusion uses a VAE-like encoder/decoder so denoising happens in a compressed image space, then the final latent is decoded to pixels.
The latent diffusion paper highlights this computational advantage. Compression helps speed and memory, but the decoded image can still have artifacts or wrong details.

blocks.analogy: Latent diffusion edits a compressed blueprint before printing the full poster.

blocks.title: Latent purpose

options.text: To reduce compute and memory while preserving useful visual structure.

blocks.explanation: Latent space is efficient, not perfect.

modules.title: Text conditioning guides the latent denoiser
modules.sub: The prompt becomes vectors that influence each step.
modules.summary: Prompt encoding steers denoising but cannot guarantee every detail.

spans.text: Stable Diffusion pipelines encode prompt text into conditioning vectors. The UNet uses those vectors while predicting denoising corrections. Higher guidance can increase prompt pressure, but too much can create harsh artifacts or brittle images.

A prompt asks for eight labeled planets. The generated image has vivid colors but six planets and unreadable labels. The model captured topic and style, not exact diagram truth; a deterministic diagram tool is safer.

modules.title: UNet predicts and scheduler steps
modules.sub: One component estimates noise; the other updates the latent.
modules.summary: The reverse process is an iterative component handoff.
objectives: Connect seed and steps to reproducibility.

blocks.title: Prediction and update are different jobs

spans.text: At each timestep, the UNet predicts the noise or correction in the current latent. The scheduler uses that prediction to compute the next latent. The seed sets the initial latent noise; steps, scheduler, and guidance shape the route.

modules.title: Code a traceable Stable Diffusion call
modules.sub: Record the settings that make the image reviewable.
modules.summary: A minimal run should save model, scheduler, seed, steps, and prompt metadata.
objectives: Read a Diffusers Stable Diffusion call.

blocks.title: Stable Diffusion run with explicit settings
blocks.code:
import torch
from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline, EulerDiscreteScheduler

model_id = "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5"
pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(model_id, torch_dtype=torch.float16)
pipe.scheduler = EulerDiscreteScheduler.from_config(pipe.scheduler.config)
pipe = pipe.to("cuda")

generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(42)
image = pipe(
    prompt="clean educational illustration of a student studying a solar-system diagram",
    negative_prompt="blurry, unreadable text, distorted hands",
    num_inference_steps=25,
    guidance_scale=7.5,
    generator=generator,
).images[0]
image.save("solar-system-study.png")

spans.text: This requires Diffusers and suitable hardware. The lesson is to record model, scheduler, seed, steps, guidance, and prompts.

predictThenReveal.prompt: What does changing only the seed usually affect?
predictThenReveal.answer: It changes initial latent noise, so composition and details may change while other settings stay the same.

spans.text: Checklist: model/license reviewed; seed, scheduler, steps, and guidance recorded; dtype/device intentional; safety review path kept; and outputs inspected for artifacts and rights.

modules.summary: Stable Diffusion assets need artifact, license, and factual checks.
objectives: Choose when generated images are inappropriate.

blocks.title: A decoded image can be efficient and wrong

spans.text: Latent diffusion can be practical and still produce distorted anatomy, false diagrams, unreadable text, identity-sensitive depictions, or rights problems. The workflow needs labels, review, and replacement rules.

blocks.ruleOfThumb: Use Stable Diffusion for visual drafts; use verified tools for exact diagrams and claims.
blocks.useWhen: Use it for concept art, mood boards, and low-risk visual exploration with review.
blocks.avoidWhen: Avoid factual diagrams, identity-sensitive images, or licensed-brand contexts without provenance and review.

diffusion.label: Diffusion
diffusion.laymanDefinition: A generative process that learns to turn noise into structured media.
diffusion.technicalNote: Diffusion systems combine denoising steps, conditioning, schedulers, and safety controls; quality and provenance depend on the full pipeline.

latent_space.label: Latent space
latent_space.laymanDefinition: A compressed representation where models manipulate meaning more efficiently than raw pixels or audio.
latent_space.technicalNote: Latent-space choices affect speed, detail, editability, artifacts, and what safety or provenance checks can inspect.

pipeline.label: Pipeline
pipeline.laymanDefinition: The ordered set of model, preprocessing, generation, postprocessing, and safety steps.
pipeline.technicalNote: Media pipelines should pin model versions, prompts, parameters, assets, moderation, watermarking, and review metadata for reproducibility.

vlm.label: VLM
vlm.laymanDefinition: A model that connects visual inputs with language understanding or generation.
vlm.technicalNote: VLM workflows need image preprocessing, prompt grounding, output validation, and privacy review for uploaded visual content.

asr.label: ASR
asr.laymanDefinition: Technology that converts spoken audio into text.
asr.technicalNote: ASR systems should track language, accent, noise, timestamps, confidence, privacy, and downstream correction paths.

provenance.label: Provenance
provenance.laymanDefinition: Evidence about where media came from and how it was created or edited.
provenance.technicalNote: Provenance for generated media includes source assets, model versions, prompts, parameters, edits, disclosures, and review decisions.
